skill.name: lookalike-accounts
skill.description: Find companies like your existing customers using company data from Leadsets. Rank matches by shared traits and exclude seed domains and any additional domains you list.
skill.summary: Turn customer domains into a ranked list of similar companies with reasons for each match.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown and business workflow terminology. The Leadsets endpoint is legitimate, but the workflow sends seed customer domains there without an explicit data-sharing check. Named exports can also expose seed identities and enriched details to destination viewers.

remediation.issue: No explicit check before customer domains are sent to Leadsets
remediation.suggestion: Identify Leadsets as the recipient and verify sharing approval before enrichment. Send only normalized company domains and keep private CRM fields and exclusions local.
Omit seed identities, seed details, and prospect-to-seed mappings by default. Confirm the destination and its audience before exporting, and require separate approval to include seed details.

content.user_title: Find Companies Like Your Best Customers
content.value_statement: Building a prospect list from scratch can miss the traits your best customers share. This skill uses Leadsets company data to find and rank similar companies, with reasons for each match.
actual_capabilities: Checks Leadsets usage limits before requesting company records.
Enriches seed domains with industry, headcount range, location, and technology.
Builds a profile from shared traits and tests the search filters with one result.
Removes seed domains, supplied exclusions, and duplicate domains.
Ranks companies by matched traits and reports the reasons and any shortfall.
Exports to CSV or writes to a named Google Sheet or CRM through an available connection.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or REST API access.
Needs at least three successfully enriched seeds to build a profile.
Leadsets coverage and usage quotas can limit the number of matches.
Returns company accounts only and does not find contacts, verify emails, or scrape websites.

use_cases.title: Build a First Target List
use_cases.description: Use approved domains from your best customers to find similar companies and review why each one ranks.

use_cases.title: Refresh Sales Accounts
use_cases.description: Use an approved customer sample to find new accounts while excluding current customers, open deals, and competitors.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Customer Profile to a New Region
use_cases.description: Keep the industry and company size from a client-approved profile while searching within a new region.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Small List
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these three company domains, approved for Leadsets, to find 20 similar companies. Show the ranked results and why each matched.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with three known customer domains.

prompt_templates.title: Exclude Known Accounts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved seed domains from this CSV to find 50 similar companies. Apply the supplied exclusions locally and export only prospect rows to CSV.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refresh a list without including current accounts or open deals.

prompt_templates.title: Search a New Region
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these approved domains to profile shared industry and headcount. Find up to 40 Canadian matches and report any filter you relax.
prompt_templates.scenario: Test the same company profile in a different market.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved seed column and check Leadsets quotas before searching for 100 matches. Present the profile and shortfall. Wait for approval before writing prospect rows to the named sheet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a team list without exporting seed details.

output_examples.input: Find 20 similar companies using three approved seed domains.
output: All three seed companies were enriched.
Shared profile: United States software companies with 50 to 200 employees.
Returned 20 ranked companies after removing seed domains and duplicates.
Northstar Analytics ranked first because it matched the industry, size, and location.

output_examples.input: Find up to 40 Canadian matches and exclude the supplied open deals.
output: Returned 32 of 40 requested companies after exclusions.
The initial search found no matches, so the technology filter was relaxed.
The final list kept the requested region and the shared industry and size.

best_practices: Choose representative customers and use only domains approved for sharing with Leadsets.
Provide existing customer, open deal, and competitor domains as exclusions.
Review the inferred profile and confirm who can access the destination before exporting.
anti_patterns: Providing full CRM rows or contact details when only company domains are needed.
Assuming all current customers are excluded when only seed domains were supplied.
Sharing seed details or prospect-to-seed links in a widely accessible export.

faq.question: How many customer domains should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide 3 to 20 company domains. At least three must return company data for the skill to build a profile.

faq.question: What makes a company a match?
faq.answer: The skill compares industry, headcount range, location, and technology. Companies rank higher when they match more traits in the seed profile.

faq.question: Are all current customers excluded?
faq.answer: Only seed domains are excluded by default. Supply the rest of your customer domains and any open deals or competitors you want excluded.

faq.question: Does the skill send my domains to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Leadsets receives each seed domain for enrichment and the derived filters for company search.

faq.question: Does the search use Leadsets records?
faq.answer: Yes. A successful enrichment or returned search result uses a record. The skill checks usage and tests its filters before requesting more results.

faq.question: Where can I put the results?
faq.answer: CSV is the default. A named Google Sheet or CRM requires an available connection. Review access before exporting seed details.
